title: Temper the fifth, find the wolf
intro: A keyboard has twelve keys to the octave, but stacking pure fifths (3:2, 701.96 cents) never comes back to the starting note, and four pure fifths give a third much wider than the pure 5:4. Meantone temperament narrows every fifth by a fraction of the syntonic comma (21.51 cents) to bring the thirds closer to pure. Choose the fraction: 0 is Pythagorean tuning with pure fifths. Watch the major third C–E, how fast it beats against the pure third, and the one fifth left over between G♯ and E♭ on a keyboard tuned from E♭ to G♯: the wolf. Listen to the C major chord and to the wolf fifth.
fraction: Fifths narrowed by (fraction of the syntonic comma)
